title: Zygote to blastocyst: cleavage, morula and hatching
description: Explore early conceptus divisions, compaction, blastomeres, blastocoel, inner cell mass, trophoblast and hatching before implantation.

questions.question: What does cleavage do to a newly formed zygote?
questions.answer: It produces more, initially smaller, blastomeres while the conceptus remains within the zona pellucida. Early divisions do not require the whole sphere to grow much larger at every division.

questions.question: How is a morula different from a blastocyst?
questions.answer: A morula is a compact solid cluster. A blastocyst has a fluid-filled blastocoel, an outer cell layer and a localized inner cell mass; the illustration depicts the latter, not every earlier stage.

questions.question: What does the inner cell mass become?
questions.answer: Its descendants contribute to the embryo proper and certain extraembryonic structures. A blastocyst cell cluster is not a miniature fully formed fetus.

questions.question: Why does the blastocyst hatch from the zona pellucida?
questions.answer: Loss of the extracellular zona permits trophoblast contact with receptive uterine endometrium. A conceptus still enclosed by the zona is not already embedded in uterine tissue.

questions.question: Does a blastocyst in the uterus mean pregnancy has implanted?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. Arrival in the uterine cavity and hatching precede attachment to endometrium; implantation is a separate stage with variable timing.
